Which method should I use?

EML: Use your mail client's download / save-message option, then select the original EML file. The importer decodes MIME, base64 and quoted-printable parts.

Rich paste: Copy the message normally and paste below. If the clipboard includes HTML, its link destinations are kept as source text.

HTML: Import the saved HTML message when EML is unavailable. TXT and plain-text paste cannot recover hidden links. PDF, images and Outlook MSG are not supported.

Files fill the editor and analyze a new message, replacing its current inputs. Failed imports leave the current message untouched.

Plain-text input may omit button destinations. Import EML or paste rich HTML for better coverage.

More context for stronger checks

A deterministic screening tool, not a probability model or a security guarantee. English and selected Chinese phrases are recognized. A low score does not establish safety.

How the decision is made

Each rule contributes once. Related evidence is capped by category, then category totals are added and capped at 100.

0–19: Few detected signals. 20–49: Review required. 50–100: High risk. These are design thresholds, not calibrated probabilities.

Authentication results are pasted claims, never independently verified. Passing results do not subtract points. Missing information lowers coverage, not the risk score.
